inspection: Parse actual NPK parts and FILE_CONTAINER; compare embedded SquashFS bytes to cached system.squashfs.
Read numeric on-image SquashFS inventory; stream keyman/mode/loader anew with unsquashfs -cat; verify equality with cached extracts and prior hashes.
Count exact configured LICENSE 32-byte literals across every unique regular inode traversed in each extracted SquashFS; skip symlinks and deduplicate hardlinks.

Revalidate six pinned candidates from previous evidence against current pristine bytes: decode raw ARM condition/opcode/register/literal-address/rotated-ADD fields, reconstruct original words privately, check store mnemonics and source/base/displacement operands using Capstone, and compare privately to configured vendor public role.

Exhaustively scan all executable PROGBITS sections for PC-relative LDR references targeting each literal pool offset, direct branch/call targets (B, BL, BLX) into the envelope, calls inside the envelope, and relocation entries in .rel.dyn/.rel.plt.

Directly run current patch_npk_package with LICENSE-only mapping to a synthetic 32-byte sentinel, capturing tool output privately. Repeat under Python -O with LICENSE and signing public roles mapped to two synthetic nonsecret sentinels. Do not read custom/private keys, call signing or save firmware. TemporaryDirectory extraction and temporary generic signing-pattern replacement are cleaned on failure.
method.limitations: No replacement instruction encoding designed or applied, no source suite rerun, no vendor signature validation, no exhaustive kernel/initramfs semantic audit, no real device or emulator runtime test.

bounded_matcher_feasibility_analysis.offline_research_scope_only: Not production-integrated, no source edits, no bypass.

literal_pool_isolation.result: Fresh enumeration of aligned A32 immediate PC-relative LDR encodings in executable PROGBITS finds exactly one such reference to each of 7 slots (9 in arm/loader), inside the candidate envelope. No extra direct LDR references were observed in that specific encoding class. Whole-file exact little-endian absolute pool-address searches and REL/RELA relocation-target checks also returned zero.
literal_pool_isolation.decoder_caution: A single aligned immediate PC-relative LDR scan is NOT proof of the absence of indirect, computed, register-relative, or Thumb-interworked aliases. A linear 4-byte ARM disassembly sweep across .text encounters 35 to 52 decode failures per binary due to inline literal pools, embedded data, or non-ARM fragments; a full control flow graph with mapping symbols ($a, $t, $d) would be required to prove exclusive pool ownership.

proposed_offline_mutation_allowlist_not_.literal_mutations: Only the seven four-byte literal-pool words supplying raw32 indices 0,1,2,4,5,6,7 (or nine canonical limb slots supplying 0..7,9 in arm/loader). No LDR addressing, destination register, condition, stores, call, stack arithmetic, ELF tables, branch targets or file lengths may change.
proposed_offline_mutation_allowlist_not_.arithmetic_mutations: Only immediate encoding bits in the three existing AL non-S ADD instructions in the derived r3 chain, retaining opcode ADD, Rn=Rd=r3, condition, S bit and instruction size. Validate modified-immediate roundtrip and a delta solver; reject unencodable candidates rather than insert instructions. No solver or mutation was implemented/tested here.
proposed_offline_mutation_allowlist_not_.expected_register_results: For raw32: r6/r7 hold replacement words4/5, r3 stores word2 then derives word3, r0/r1 first store words0/1 then words6/7; final STRD writes r6/r7 to sp+16/+20. ARM mode instead uses r3 sequentially for words0..7 at r4-840..-812. For arm loader r3 sequentially stores canonical limbs0..9 at sp+264..300; limb8 derives from loaded limb7. Intermediate r3 values may change only when proven unobserved except final derived store.
proposed_offline_mutation_allowlist_not_.extra_uses_and_call_limits: ARM keyman and all three arm64 targets load r6/r7 before BL and store them after BL. Their ABI preservation and callee use are not audited: callees may save/read them even if convention preserves them. Post-construction LDM/STM reads/copies buffer content and aliases stack addresses; this must be traced. ARM mode has no call and r3 is only used by its stores and ADD chain inside the envelope, making it the simpler bounded offline candidate, not yet verified production integration.
proposed_offline_mutation_allowlist_not_.release_constraint: Any future package policy must demand complete pinned keyman/mode/loader treatment and separate runtime evidence, not merely exploit current per-package minimum-one coverage. No loader preservation rule or production integration is justified by this audit.

instruction_budget_and_arithmetic_repres.derived_word_bottleneck: Seven words are loaded directly from literal pools. The eighth word is NOT stored in a pool; it is computed at runtime via three consecutive ADD instructions with rotated 8-bit immediates applied to a loaded pool word.
instruction_budget_and_arithmetic_repres.replacement_implication: Potential encoding constraint only: if restricted to changing the three existing ADD immediate fields, the replacement derived-word delta must be expressible as three ARM modified-immediate constants modulo 2^32. This audit did NOT read or test the actual custom-key difference, run a solver, or prove any particular replacement unencodable. Alternative reviewed instruction plans are outside this audit; no claim that adding instructions is the only possible solution.
instruction_budget_and_arithmetic_repres.conclusion: A potential offline matcher cannot assume arbitrary key representability without an encoding preflight check for the arithmetic chain.

control_flow_and_calls_inside_envelope.impact: In 4 of the 6 targets, subroutine calls occur while intermediate key components are in registers or on the stack. The matcher cannot treat the instruction envelope as a simple contiguous basic block.

guard_and_source_findings.interpretation: The licensing value is present in reconstructed form; missing literal coverage is not key absence. Signing-role hits cannot satisfy the distinct required LICENSE mapping. The guard correctly blocks both packages, including with assertions disabled.

implementation_readiness.answer: Pinned static extraction is feasible and six candidates are revalidated. That is not a verified transformation or runtime policy. Neither architecture can honestly be declared bare-metal/licensing ready from the available evidence, and no bypass is justified.
blockers: No production ARM32 or AArch64 matcher. Needed: strict ELF/code-boundary validation and complete original-buffer matching, not independent four-byte word substitution.

Prove literal-pool ownership and all references, live register/use-def effects, aliases, relocation interactions, branch/call paths, and Thumb boundaries before modifying pools or arithmetic. Previous single PC-load reference counts are not complete alias/control-flow proof.

Derived words use ARM rotated-immediate ADD encodings; arbitrary replacement deltas are not guaranteed encodable in the same instruction budget. No replacement simulation, representability proof or instruction roundtrip tests were run.
ARM loader has canonical ten-limb form while ARM64-package loader reconstructs raw32. Need distinct representation handling and canonical/carry/encoding tests, not architecture-name assumptions.
No ARM/ARM64 paired runtime evidence determines whether loader anchors must change or be preserved. The CHR i386 loader exception cannot be copied to RouterBOARD or ARM64.

Need synthetic positive/negative/overlap/conditional/alias/malformed ELF tests, reviewed fail-closed production integration, real SquashFS metadata parity and signature checks without weakening coverage.

Need identified supported hardware, RouterBOOT version/settings, compatible recovery path and matched vendor baseline before isolated install, cold boot, login and legitimate licensing/upgrade persistence tests.

CPU ISA support is not universal board/product compatibility. No evidence validates arbitrary ARM SBC/UEFI systems, every RouterBOARD model, or every screenshot architecture. TILE, MIPS and PPC are outside this audit.

official_documented_facts: MikroTik hardware routers running RouterOS come preinstalled with a RouterOS license; ordinary owners do not need a custom activation key.
x86 PC licensing requires a license key associated with its Software ID; CHR has a different System ID/licensing product. CHR p-unlimited evidence is not RouterBOARD activation evidence.

Official licensing page describes RouterBOARD Software ID as bound to storage media, x86 Software ID to MBR, and CHR System ID to MBR and UUID. Embedded MikroTik hardware licenses cannot be moved to a new system.
Netinstall reformats the system drive and loses configuration/user files, but does not erase the RouterOS license key or reset RouterBOOT settings.

For the documented RouterBOARD Netinstall workflow, the device must enter Etherboot/network-boot mode, with appropriate architecture packages, a configured installation host and an appropriate Ethernet/L2 path. Device reset/boot methods and Etherboot port follow the specific model manual; regular and backup booter behavior matters. This is not a universal RouterBOARD-only restriction on Netinstall; x86 Netinstall is a separate supported workflow.
RouterBOOT can select network boot, or the documented reset/serial procedures can enter Etherboot. Protected RouterBOOT and other settings require model-specific review.
engineering_conclusions_not_vendor_unive: For a RouterBOARD deployment of these standalone ARM/ARM64 NPKs, identify the supported model and validate its RouterBOOT/recovery process. Arbitrary-board compatibility is UNVERIFIED: this audit did not inventory all DTBs, bootloaders or board drivers and does not prove their absence. A CPU architecture label alone does not establish board support. Netinstall also supports x86 installation; RouterBOARD/RouterBOOT requirements here describe the scoped RouterBOARD deployment, not every Netinstall use.
Netinstall is an installer/recovery method, not a license generator or a method that makes arbitrary ARM boards supported. NPK alone is not an ISO or complete universal disk image.

The audited standalone arm64 NPK, any CHR ARM64 disk image, and an installer ISO are distinct artifact/product scopes. No CHR ARM64 image or ISO was inspected, installed, or validated by this audit. Each requires its own documented support, provenance and runtime validation; results for this NPK cannot be transferred to them.

No RouterBOOT signature enforcement, downgrade restrictions, protected-boot behavior, or patched-package acceptance was tested. Do not weaken secure boot/signature policy to obtain a successful install.

release_conclusion: Blocked for an ARM/ARM64-ready NEW v1 claim. Preserve fail-closed coverage and report exact unsupported scope. x86 image readiness is outside this audit; existing CHR evidence does not validate bare-metal ARM/ARM64 or x86 installers. No release action taken.
